Israeli ambassador sees Left Party victory in Berlin as danger to Jews

blocks.caption: Ron Prosor is seen here at a DW interviewImage: Simon Young/DW

blocks.text: The Israeli ambassador to Germany, Ron Prosor, says the win by the socialist Left Party at Berlin state elections on Sunday poses a "direct existential danger" for the Jewish community in the German capital.
"The strong performance of the Left at the Berlin elections should worry anyone who cherishes the continued existence of Jewish life in this city," he told the German DPA news agency.
"The completely unbridled antisemitism that has manifested itself in this party has been given a new political dimension by its rise to the strongest force," Prosor said.
Elif Eralp, the Left's top candidate who might become the governing mayor of Berlin, has said that antisemitism was not stronger in her party than in society at large.
"The overwhelming majority of the party is clearly in favor of protecting Jewish life and the strength of Jewish life," she said at a discussion run by the Jewish Community in Berlin (JGzB).
"Antisemitism is a problem in society in general and exists also within the Left Party," she said.
